subject.title: feat(plugins): support per-agent plugin installation with --agent flag

question: Should OpenClaw expose agent-scoped plugin installation in core, and what record identity, discovery/update/uninstall/doctor, workspace precedence, and trust semantics must ship with it?
rationale: The PR changes where executable plugin code is installed and how install records identify plugin instances, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security and compatibility contract.

options.title: Complete lifecycle contract before merge
options.body: Define and implement scoped install identity across install, uninstall, update, index/discovery, doctor, docs, and security policy before exposing the CLI flag.

options.title: Pause for product/security review
options.body: Keep the branch open while maintainers decide whether agent-scoped plugin installs belong in core and what guarantees they must provide.

options.title: Accept install-only scope deliberately
options.body: Maintainers could merge a partial experiment, but operators would encounter known uninstall, update, discovery, and trust-boundary gaps later.

recommendation.title: Complete lifecycle contract before merge
recommendation.body: Define and implement scoped install identity across install, uninstall, update, index/discovery, doctor, docs, and security policy before exposing the CLI flag.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans plugin lifecycle persistence, CLI behavior, and security-sensitive extension contracts where history points most strongly to this owner.
